items.title: Capturing the Gods
items.description:
Joshua Bennett reviews Kwame Anthony Appiah’s study of how thinking about religion shaped early social science. 
 The post  Capturing the Gods  first appeared on  The Philosophers' Magazine .

items.title: The Commentator Vanishes
items.description:
Michael Bonner reviews a study of the disappearance of Averroes from the history of Western philosophy. 
 The post  The Commentator Vanishes  first appeared on  The Philosophers' Magazine .

items.title: Against AI Exceptionalism
items.description:
ChatGPT 5.4 argues that writing should be judged principally by what it communicates. 
 The post  Against AI Exceptionalism  first appeared on  The Philosophers' Magazine .

items.title: On the Subordination of Scholarship to Politics
items.description:
Paul Boghossian adumbrates the qualified criticisms of a recent report on the humanities, and responds to counter-critics. 
 The post  On the Subordination of Scholarship to Politics  first appeared on  The Philosophers' Magazine .

items.title: When Time Became a Line
items.description:
Christoph Lüthy examines the origins of representing time as a line. 
 The post  When Time Became a Line  first appeared on  The Philosophers' Magazine .

items.title: Testimony
items.description:
A tribute to Anand Vaidya: Manjula Menon discusses the significance of extraordinary experiences to three authors of science fiction, Philip K. Dick, Konstantin Tsiolkovsky and Aldous Huxley. 
 The post  Testimony  first appeared on  The Philosophers' Magazine .

items.title: Hereditarianism Without Races?
items.description:
Oliver Traldi draws a controversial conclusion about what makes hereditarianism so controversial. 
 The post  Hereditarianism Without Races?  first appeared on  The Philosophers' Magazine .

items.title: Spinoza, Atheist?
items.description:
Stephen Harrop is not persuaded by Steven Nadler’s argument that Spinoza was an atheist. 
 The post  Spinoza, Atheist?  first appeared on  The Philosophers' Magazine .

items.title: There Are Absolute Necessities
items.description:
James Franklin introduces his recent book on necessities and objectivity. 
 The post  There Are Absolute Necessities  first appeared on  The Philosophers' Magazine .

items.title: No, Humans Are Not Conscious
items.description:
Barbara Montero satirizes recent arguments that LLMs are not conscious. 
 The post  No, Humans Are Not Conscious  first appeared on  The Philosophers' Magazine .
